beats.text: You avoid deep talks because you think they'll be awkward. They're not!
In twelve experiments, strangers were paired up. Some got small talk questions. Others got deep ones.
Like: when did you last cry in front of someone?
First, they predicted how awkward it would be. Then they talked.
Far less awkward than expected! And the deep talks felt closer and more fun.
People also underestimated how interested the other person was in them.
So skip the weather. Ask the real question.

ask: WHAT'S YOUR BEST DEEP QUESTION? COMMENT.
sources: Kardas, Kumar & Epley (2021), Overly shallow? Miscalibrated expectations create a barrier to deeper conversation, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology – 12 experiments, more than 1,800 participants, mostly pairs of strangers; deep and shallow conversations were both less awkward than predicted, deep ones especially; deep conversations were more enjoyable and created more connection; people underestimated how interested their partner would be in them.
